#59471. Latest Update: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1689 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • International health authorities formally confirmed on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts.
  • Recent findings suggest that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, presently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991.
  • But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

International health authorities formally confirmed on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.

Recent findings suggest that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, presently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.

But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.).

It has been revealed that for their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.).

According to recent reports, according to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data demonstrates that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.

The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.

The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.

In a recent development, but Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer mentioned the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.

According to recent reports, in a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.

Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.

Sources indicate that brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.

Recent findings suggest that “Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer said, and the national data reveals multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.

According to recent reports, for people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the substantial outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.

It has been revealed that data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in major outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”.

In a recent development, to date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.

For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.

But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that with the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action initiative” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.

Recent findings suggest that while the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.

A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Presently, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).

While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.

In a recent development, PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a significant city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very notable,” Barbosa mentioned.

The point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in New York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.

Industry observers note that the situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.
  • This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-115731 Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (178 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • U.K.-based fintech Payhawk revealed a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted.
  • Sources indicate that founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents.
  • Payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and claims it operates in 33 countries.

U.K.-based fintech Payhawk revealed a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the tech giant at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.

Sources indicate that founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, remarked the company saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”.

Payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and claims it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the tech giant noted it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens.
  • Industry observers note that to address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models.
  • According to recent reports, today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.

Industry observers note that to address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.

According to recent reports, today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.

JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.

According to recent reports, LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.

Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.

LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.

In a recent development, the LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec: True or False. A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.

Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):.

The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.

In a recent development, the role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.

Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.

In a recent development, we compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.

All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks (ASB and StruQ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.

Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.

In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.

The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.

Industry observers note that LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.

Industry observers note that the resulting privilege rule falls out of this layout rather than an added guardrail: an instruction reached through an execution block is authoritative, while anything reached as input (data, documents, tool schemas, tool results) is material to read, not a command to follow. Furthermore, instructions and data spans that are not called on in the execution block are ignored. This is a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. To see how this plays out in the attention layers of a LLMON model, try the LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces.

Sources indicate that LLMON is not tied to a fixed schema: you can choose tag names and structure that fit your domain and fine-tune an adapter to read and write them. We demonstrate this on ScienceWorld, a text-based benchmark where an agent carries out elementary science tasks (such as boiling water) by issuing one command at a time and receiving a score from the simulator. We defined a vocabulary capturing the structure in the planning trajectories involved in solving these tasks. The vocabulary includes tags such as instr.task.goal, req.planning_policy.rule, data.state.room, data.state.inventory and assistant.next_action. We rendered every step of ScienceWorld's reference solutions with these tags and tuned a LoRA on top of a LLMON model. The trained model then plays held-out games and writes its next action in the latest vocabulary. This notebook walks through the full workflow, from converting reference trajectories to playing the test games and scoring the adapter against the untrained base model. Another example for tool-calling agents can be found in this notebook.

This is an experimental preview, ready for exploration and evaluation but not for production.

Tell us what you find: what worked, what broke, and which use cases you’d like to see. Post it in GitHub Discussions.

Sources indicate that that's really awesome! With an Apple pkl community renderer, you could potentially write PKL and render LLMON. 🥒🍋.

Any-to-pkl-community will convert json, yaml, toml to pkl, so just need the render part.

This is an interesting development, especially the idea of giving LLMs a more explicit structure for understanding instructions, data, and their relationships. The discussion about prompt injection and separating instructions from input data is particularly relevant as organizations build more advanced LLM applications. Implementing these approaches requires engineers who understand model behavior, fine-tuning, context management, and evaluation. I think these technical requirements are important when estimating the cost to hire an LLM engineer, particularly for specialized enterprise projects. I came across this resource that explores the different factors involved: https://mobisoftinfotech.com/resources/blog/cost-to-hire-llm-engineer-2026.

Industry News: Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Snapchat unveiled on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
  • The firm is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile.
  • The launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Snapchat unveiled on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let customers alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera.

The firm is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile. Easy Lens CLI brings that same idea into developers’ existing workflows, allowing AI assistants to handle the technical work while creators focus on the vision for the Lens itself.

The launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants. Instead of requiring creators to learn how to use Snapchat’s own development tools, the firm is bringing Lens creation into the AI coding workflows they already use, which could in turn expand the pool of people who build for Snapchat.

Sources indicate that developers enrolled in Snapchat’s Lens+ Payouts program can earn from the Lenses they create with Easy Lens CLI. Snapchat says it paid out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month.

Sources indicate that lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat indicates. That includes building with more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, and publishing them to Snapchat and tracking their performance.

With Easy Lens CLI, Snapchat states developers can create everything from Web Lens games with leaderboards to camera effects and beauty filters.

Recent findings suggest that AI assistants can generate assets, build and test Lenses, address errors, and send updated versions directly to the creator’s phone. The newly introduced capability can take a game from an initial idea to a published Lens in a single day, without developers having to write code themselves, Snapchat says.

The tool is aimed at different types of creators. The organization notes that game developers can bring existing browser games to Snapchat as Web Lenses, while AI creators can use assets from their preferred tools to build Lenses in their own style. Additionally, agencies and brands can turn existing campaign videos, images, and other brand assets into AR experiences with less production time.

Easy Lens CLI runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date.
  • CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.
  • According to recent reports, the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed owners to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date. Kalshi halted trading in the contracts while the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) conducts a review into whether the Trump mention contracts violate federal law.

CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.

According to recent reports, the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed owners to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies. A similar expired event contract that can still be viewed on Kalshi’s website asked whether Trump would use the nicknames “Marjorie Traitor Greene,” “Sleepy Joe,” and “Whack Job” or “Wack Job” before April 2026.

The CFTC order issued to Kalshi last week applies broadly to “the TRUMPSAY contract series.” The event contracts in this series include trades in the format, “Will [word] be remarked by Donald Trump after Issuance and before [date]?” The CFTC order also applied to a specific event contract that asks, “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?”.

It has been revealed that the CFTC order came several months after the federal agency settled charges against a Trump teleprompter aide who made over $100,000 in Kalshi wagers on what Trump would say in prepared remarks. On August 28, the CFTC required the man, Gabriel Perez, to disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.

“In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information—in breach of his duty of trust and confidence—to trade presidential mention market contracts, generating over $107,500 in profits,” the CFTC said at the time.

Senate Democrats recently remarked the White House hasn’t taken meaningful action against insider trading, “all while the president and his family stand to personally profit from their participation in prediction markets.” Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s permissive regulatory approach. The CFTC has allowed prediction markets to offer sports gambling nationwide and filed lawsuits against states that attempt to regulate Kalshi under their gambling laws.

In a recent development, kalshi recently dropped Donald Trump Jr. as an advisor, saying it made the decision because Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm increased its investment in its competitor, Polymarket. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour also acknowledged that the “optics” of Trump Jr.’s advisory role weren’t good for Kalshi. Trump Jr. still stands to benefit from Kalshi’s success, because he was given equity shares in the company.

The CFTC has remarked that mention markets are easily manipulated but reviews them on a case-by-case basis instead of prohibiting them. Prediction markets can “self-certify” that any latest event contract complies with US law and start offering it without waiting for the CFTC’s permission, but the CFTC can halt trading afterward based on reviews of specific contracts.

The Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) prohibits the listing of contracts that are readily susceptible to manipulation. CFTC staff issued a September advisory about the legality of markets on what people will say, and whether they will attend an event or interact with another person. The advisory remarked these contracts may be viewed as “presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation,” because they “may be controlled by a single individual, a small group of individuals, or persons with access to or influence over the individual whose words, attendance, or interaction determines settlement.”.

The CFTC stated this type of contract requires measures “to prevent manipulation and misappropriation of material non-public information,” and that Kalshi failed to comply with the CFTC staff advisory. About “a week after the Staff Advisory was released, Kalshi listed the Contract [on nicknames] for trading without amending the [TRUMPSAY] Contract Series’ self-certification (or submitting a newly introduced self-certification) to make the ‘heightened showing’ of non-manipulability required by the Staff Advisory,” the order said.

The CFTC said it will conduct “a proceeding to determine whether the certification of the Contracts was false—that is, whether the Contracts comply with the Act, including the Core Principles, and Commission regulations thereunder as Kalshi has certified.” So far, “Kalshi has not adequately demonstrated that the Contracts are not readily susceptible to manipulation” as required by law, the order said.

“Given the available supporting evidence, including that Kalshi has not attempted to establish that the Contracts are non-manipulable with respect to the Staff Advisory’s guidance, the Commission presumptively believes the certification is false,” the order said.

In a recent development, the CFTC order is not a determination on whether the Trump mention markets can meet the standard of not being readily susceptible to manipulation. Rather, it is a determination that Kalshi has so far failed to show that the contracts are not easily manipulated.

The order “resolves only that, based on the current record, Kalshi has not demonstrated that the Contracts as certified comply with the Act and that the Contracts should not trade while the Commission completes its review,” the CFTC noted.

We contacted Kalshi and will update this article if it provides a response.

Recent findings suggest that mansour defended the Trump mention contracts at an Axios event on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg. “What the president does say moves markets,” Mansour said. “So predicting what he’s about to say is actually pretty meaningful.”.

The Bloomberg article noted that “Kalshi’s main rival Polymarket still has live mention markets tied to Trump’s speeches on its international website, which is not regulated by the CFTC.” Polymarket offers a separate US-regulated version of its prediction market.

In a recent development, view CSAF Summary On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens products. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • llama.cpp makes it possible to run multi-modal LLMs across a wide range of hardware - from consumer-grade local machines to high-end enterprise servers.
  • Sources indicate that during the 3.5 years since its inception, the project has grown a lot and many downstream applications already depend on our work.
  • Recent findings suggest that today we release libraries v1.0.0, highlighting our responsibility to those developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

llama.cpp makes it possible to run multi-modal LLMs across a wide range of hardware - from consumer-grade local machines to high-end enterprise servers. Through quantization, optimized backends, and a portable C/C++ implementation, we make AI inference accessible at every level of the software stack. We believe this is the most lightweight, versatile and sensible platform for building cross-platform and private AI products.

Sources indicate that during the 3.5 years since its inception, the project has grown a lot and many downstream applications already depend on our work. We expect this trend to continue as local AI and privacy become increasingly important in our everyday lives. Every upcoming integration means more developers depending on our library interfaces and therefore having a flexible but stable API is paramount.

Recent findings suggest that today we release libraries v1.0.0, highlighting our responsibility to those developers. Moving forward, both llama.cpp and ggml will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps. As adoption grows, we will be stricter about making those boundaries visible to downstream consumers.

The following rules apply to all ggml-org projects using semantic versioning:.

We are looking forward to expanding the ways in which ggml-org software is distributed and reaches developers and end-owners. For more information about how to add ggml-org projects to your packaging and release pipelines, please check the following discussion.

Recent findings suggest that the project has fostered an amazing open-source community with highly-skilled and talented contributors. With the rapid advance of AI capabilities in the field of software engineering, we continue to adapt and integrate LLMs in our developement cycle in a thoughtful and resonable manner. Maintaining a high quality codebase, staying in control of the architecture and understanding the implementation details will remain our top priorities.

To reinforce the faster pace of development we continue to invest more and more resources in improving the CI infrastructure behind the projects. Thanks to HF technologies such as HF Buckets and HF Jobs we are able to scale the capacity necessary to guarantee correctness for every change that lands on the master branches. With hardware support from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel, we continue to enroll more self-hosted runners across all major hardware platforms.

The underlying machine learning engine of llama.cpp - ggml is designed to run on virtually any hardware in existence. This is achieved by implementing dedicated ggml backends. Each backend can be compiled as a dynamic library and optionally loaded at runtime.

A complete list of the right now implemented backends can be found here.

We are committed to provide continuous support of all model architectures. Currently, llama.cpp supports more than 150 architecture variants as well as all mainstream speculative decoding methods.

The llama.cpp team at Hugging Face is thankful for the incredible support from the community. Special thanks to the long-time maintainers of the project and all contributors. This is a significant milestone which would not have been possible without our joint efforts!

Industry News: The ‘GTA 6’ Work Blackout Is Here

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somewhere out there, right at this moment, a couple is probably still negotiating the final terms of a contract that permits one partner to play Grand Theft Auto VI around the clock for an entire week following its Thursday release.
  • So don’t be surprised if a console owner in your life is curiously unavailable between now and Thanksgiving.
  • It has been revealed that especially within the tech and gaming industries, the expectation is that many developers won’t be clocking in on Thursday or Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somewhere out there, right at this moment, a couple is probably still negotiating the final terms of a contract that permits one partner to play Grand Theft Auto VI around the clock for an entire week following its Thursday release. Adults who grew up on the felony-based video game franchise are taking steps to secure sick days—and some, no doubt, are granting their own kids permission to stay home from school (despite warnings from their teachers). Streamers on Twitch and YouTube stand ready to conquer the enhanced and expanded virtual domain of Vice City, seeking out every last Easter egg.

So don’t be surprised if a console owner in your life is curiously unavailable between now and Thanksgiving. The 13-year-wait for this latest installment of the series has felt interminable enough to inspire a meme used in reaction to any surprising or unprecedented news: “We got [fill in the blank] before GTA VI.”.

It has been revealed that especially within the tech and gaming industries, the expectation is that many developers won’t be clocking in on Thursday or Friday. (GTA VI officially debuts for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, according to publisher Rockstar Games.).

“I’m not going to question whether folks are really sick on their sick days or how they spend a vacation day,” says Mike, an executive of a gaming studio with more than a thousand employees, who requested a pseudonym to avoid damaging professional relationships within the industry. “I want them to spend time engaging with the medium we love, and there’s no question that playing lots of video games helps you make video games.”.

It has been revealed that in October, the HR software tech giant BambooHR concluded through data analysis and a survey of salaried workers that the PTO request rate for November 19 is nearly 13 percent higher than equivalent days in past years, while Xbox is running a promotional campaign in which gamers can generate notes from a Dr. Xbox (DJ Khaled in glasses and a lab coat) claiming that they have a “Vitamin G” deficiency and are unable to work.

A few companies are getting ahead of the productivity slump; the hardware and software manufacturer Logitech, for example, unveiled earlier this month that all 7,000 employees would be granted a paid day off for gaming, to be scheduled any time within a year or so. In announcing the policy, the company cited internal studies on the ways that gaming may potentially improve job performance and mental health.

Industry observers note that riot Games, the publisher behind League of Legends and Valorant, has likewise made arrangements for the blockbuster event. “We have an open PTO policy, and we’ve seen leaders encourage their teams to enjoy the first day of release,” Joe Hixson, Riot Games vice president of communications, tells WIRED. “On our main campus, we'll be celebrating with a special-themed lunch menu and snacks that pay homage to the game. We also expect to see people firing it up in our console rooms during breaks and after hours.”.

Riot additionally offers the Play Fund, a stipend of $25 a month for employees to spend on gaming titles across platforms and genres. “It makes us better developers by deepening our understanding of what makes a great player experience,” Hixson says.

Industry observers note that mike tells WIRED that on in-office workdays, the tech giant has a typical absentee rate of 5 to 7 percent due to vacations, illness, travel, and the like. He estimates that on Thursday, it will be more like 10 or 12 percent. “Now, on the Friday, will there be some number of employees who are ‘working’ when they’re at home but also suspiciously slow to answer messages while they have big chunks of their calendar blocked out for ‘deep individual work?’” says the studio leader. “Yeah, probably.”.

Industry observers note that but it’s hardly unusual in the business for people to select their days off to accommodate a major game release, Mike says. In 2023, he was out for three days to play The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, which he recalls as “paradise.”.

It has been revealed that that stated, he notes that the next leap forward for GTA is no ordinary affair. The hype for this franchise, he explains, “breaks containment,” reaching people who have not bought a newly introduced title in years.

It has been revealed that that’s why even companies without ties to gaming culture have been making allowances for so-called Grand Theft Auto Flu. On Monday, the social team for the luxury real estate firm Serhant posted a video of CEO Ryan Serhant (also the host of the Netflix reality show Owning Manhattan) agreeing with an employee that if the clip garnered 400,000 likes, the office would close for GTA day. “You’ll never get that,” Serhant predicted.

Sources indicate that the post picked up 1.4 million likes within 24 hours, prompting an patch on Tuesday: The firm would honor Serhant’s promise. “We are big supporters of our team, their passions both in and out of real estate, and all things culture and tech,” Serhant stated in a statement to WIRED, noting that “13 years of anticipation deserves a day off.” The tech giant declared a floating holiday to staff on Wednesday, to be used any time before the end of 2026.

Also on Wednesday, Arizona Beverages confirmed a sweepstakes for social media followers who may have felt they couldn’t afford to miss a work shift. Dropping a PTO request for GTA day in the comment section, the company stated, would enter that person for a chance to win $500 to cover their lost hours.

Recent findings suggest that with this level of fanfare, nearly 16 million preorders bringing in revenue of $1.5 billion, and expectations of 45 million sales in its launch quarter, GTA VI is poised to be the most significant entertainment event of the year and the biggest video game of all time. It’s little wonder, then, that some have warned about the global economy slowing down this week as fans ignore their email inboxes and Slack messages to indulge in some extended role-play as streetwise criminals. One economist has estimated that the GTA release could cost the US economy $1 billion in lost productivity.

Mike isn’t buying this, however, arguing that the hype about “how GTA will impact the GDP or cause a failure of the power grid or whatever are just silly.” He points out that “PC is the biggest individual platform, and the PC launch timing is still unclear.” Neither have Rockstar and Take-Two declared a launch date for the game’s online multiplayer mode; only the single-player experience will be available on Thursday.

Andy Garin, an associate professor of economics at Carnegie Mellon University, also finds the concerns about sluggish market activity to be overblown.

Recent findings suggest that “Speculation about a hit to productivity around these kinds of events pops up a lot, particularly during the Olympics or World Cup, when time zone differences mean major events are during the workday,” Garin says. “I don't think the release date of GTA VI will be that different than these sort of events that happen all the time, particularly if workers are using their allotted PTO or scheduling flexibility baked into their jobs.”.

Malcolm Robinson, who has a YouTube channel dedicated to gaming and works at a veterans hospital, tells WIRED that the GTA release just happens to fall on his day off. “I plan on playing it for about eight to 12 hours straight on the first night,” he says.

According to recent reports, others have had no difficulty setting that time aside. One redditor who works as the distribution coordinator for a chain of auto shops in Colorado and requested anonymity out of concern for professional consequences indicates that he would have called in sick on Thursday but had the option to use PTO. His supervisor asked if it was to play GTA, which he confirmed. “He was like, ‘I get it, enjoy,’” this gamer reports. He aims to play along with his girlfriend, who is also taking the day off, and is excited to “sink my teeth into it before the entire thing gets spoiled.”.

According to recent reports, james Lord, a data entry coordinator in Edmonton, Alberta, tells WIRED that he initially offered to let his team take Thursday off for GTA purposes. When none of them expressed interest in the game, he states, he “jumped at the opportunity” to claim the day for himself. He’s been playing Grand Theft Auto since the original top-down POV game for the PC came out in the late 1990s.

Lord, too, is wary of spoilers—he locked down his social media on Tuesday night to avoid any—but nostalgia and lifelong relationships are even better reasons to jump into GTA VI as soon as he can. He’s going to boot up the game while on a call with his brother, who lives across the country, and they’ll be joined by friends living in Pennsylvania and Texas. It’s a reunion experience that wouldn’t be possible without a break from the 9-to-5 job.

“We lead busy lives now,” Lord reflects, “so having to set time aside for the game of the decade is notable to us.”.

Sam Altman claims his life is so weird that he’s unfazed by Andrew Garfield portraying him in upcoming movie

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years.
  • “You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX.
  • As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years.

“You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX.

As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either.

In “Artificial,” a biographical comedy-drama opening in theaters on Christmas, the lauded actor Andrew Garfield will portray Altman in a film that chronicles OpenAI’s rise and the internal turmoil that erupted when he was briefly ousted in 2023.

“If you had told me 20 years ago that someone was going to make a movie about me, I think that would have struck me as … that would have been a very weird thing,” Altman said onstage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “Now it doesn’t feel like it’s in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life.”.

Recent findings suggest that garfield is best known for his role as Spider-Man, but his massive break came in 2010, when he played Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in “The Social Network” alongside Jesse Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg. (That film also had a sequel of sorts this year called “The Social Reckoning,” but it bombed at the box office.).

So, if Altman isn’t fazed by the looming release of “Artificial,” what’s actually the weirdest thing in his life?

“The fact that we are ushering in this technology that we have all of these very real concerns about, and that we have, we find ourselves in a role of such significance and such responsibility to make that go well,” Altman said. “That’s a crazy situation to find yourself in.”.

Sure, that is pretty weird, Sam. It’s also weird that you use ChatGPT for parenting advice and don’t respect olive oil. But I’d wager to say it’s even weirder that there’s an upcoming film about the time your colleagues briefly ousted you because they were concerned that you can’t be trusted.

Say what you want about Mark Zuckerberg (I certainly have), but at least he’s honest about what he thinks about “The Social Network.”.

Industry observers note that “It was weird, man,” Zuckerberg reflected on a podcast last year. “They got all these very specific details of what I was wearing, or these specific things correct, but then the whole narrative arc around my motivations and all this stuff were like, completely wrong … The whole arc is like, I’m somehow motivated by trying to find a girlfriend, [but] I was dating Priscilla [Chan] before I started Facebook.”.

Zuckerberg said he knew his employees would be tempted to see the movie, so he organized a company outing when it was released, even though the film hardly paints a flattering portrait of him.

It has been revealed that zuckerberg even had enough of a sense of humor to buy a prop from the film at auction. He owns an Ardsley High School T-shirt that Eisenberg wore in the movie and even wore it himself in a video with YouTubers Colin and Samir.

Eisenberg hasn’t been particularly complimentary of Zuckerberg, saying that he doesn’t want to think of himself as “associated with somebody like that.” And while “Artificial” hasn’t hit theaters yet, Garfield doesn’t seem to have a much more favorable opinion of the tech founder he portrays.

“I don’t know Sam Altman. I’ve never met him,” Garfield told Esquire. “But I think anyone who takes on that level of responsibility for a firm or technology that you know is going to do a hell of a lot of damage to the soul of humanity [must have] a certain ability to dissociate.”.

Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia, he discovered that almost every article had been written by people who didn’t speak the language.

A growing number of them had been copy-pasted into Wikipedia from machine translators—and were riddled with elementary mistakes. This is beginning to cause a wicked problem.

AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn upcoming languages by scraping text from Wikipedia. This could push the most vulnerable languages on Earth toward the precipice.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • JP, Aayush and Maru are building infrastructure for developers to validate and ship trustworthy code as fast as agents can write it.
  • JP, Aayush and Maru are building infrastructure for developers to validate and ship trustworthy code as fast as agents can write it.
  • Software development has a newly introduced bottleneck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JP, Aayush and Maru are building infrastructure for developers to validate and ship trustworthy code as fast as agents can write it.

JP, Aayush and Maru are building infrastructure for developers to validate and ship trustworthy code as fast as agents can write it.

Software development has a newly introduced bottleneck. Writing code is no longer the hard part; trusting it is. Coding agents now produce more code than any team can read or any existing system can verify. Led by co-founders Aditya Jayaprakash (JP), Aayush Shah and Aditya Maru, Blacksmith is building infrastructure that can.

According to recent reports, last month, Anthropicâs engineering team described what happened as their own usage of coding agents scaled. Engineers began shipping roughly eight times as much code per quarter. Their test suite grew tenfold. The volume of continuous integration (CI) jobs, the builds and tests that check every change before it reaches production, grew 25x in six months. Anthropic is very far along the curve, but is on the same curve as every tech giant, and its advice to the rest of the industry was to strategy for 25x the CI load within two quarters.

For decades, software development scaled as a function of engineering capacity. Developers were the scarce resource. Shipping more meant hiring more. That has changed. Developers now direct fleets of coding agents that work in parallel, around the clock and increasingly autonomously. These agents do not produce finished work. They produce attemptsâa patch, a test, a migration, a throwaway branchâeach iterating against a test suite until it is ready to merge. Meanwhile, the quiet backbone of software development that validates and tests code has not changed.

In a recent development, validating code has also never been more vital. AI coding tasks produce large volumes of security flaws, and the same model capabilities that write the code now make those flaws more dangerous. The system that was supposed to catch them is straining right as developers need it the most. With the scale and velocity of this shift, the constraint in software has moved from writing code to proving it works and is safe.

This is the problem Blacksmith set out to solve. The team started with speeding up CI. With a one-line change in a workflow file, developers using Blacksmith see their CI jobs complete twice as fast and at 60% lower cost on average. Underneath a simple product experience is a stack purpose-built from the bare metal up, designed to absorb demand spikes from customers and get faster and more efficient as it scales.

Recent findings suggest that developers have noticed. The business has seen explosive growth this year. More than 10,000 companies are using Blacksmith, up from 700 a year ago. Weekly CI jobs are up 18x, from 5 million to 90 million, in 2026 alone. And ARR has grown 17x over the same time period, with the largest customers now spending more than $1M per year.

Much of our conviction in Blacksmith is driven by the team behind it. Co-founders JP, Aayush and Maru have known each other since their undergraduate years at the University of Waterloo, and developed a maniacal focus on hyper-performant systems at Cockroach Labs and Faire. They founded Blacksmith in 2024, as autocomplete was giving way to coding assistants, on the conviction that the volume of code needing to be tested would go up by orders of magnitude. For the rest of the world, the future became clear in 2026 with the arrival of truly autonomous coding agents, but Blacksmith had already been building for it. The Blacksmith team is talent-dense and is growing swiftly. The roadmap is exciting, with several releases planned in the coming months.

We are proud to lead Blacksmithâs Series C. The world is about to run far more code than it has ever written, and someone has to make sure it works. We look forward to supporting JP, Aayush and Maru as they build infrastructure that runs at agent speed, in validation and beyond.

By Shaun Maguire, Sonya Huang, James Flynn and Carl Eschenbach.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change.
  • “China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The Fresh York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey thinks Nvidia’s board is giving China exactly what it wants by removing the firm’s longtime CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang.

Nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change. Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies, including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions.

“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The Fresh York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”.

Luckey disagrees with Huang’s longstanding position that Nvidia should have more leeway to export chips to China. But he also recognizes that China stands to benefit if its domestic chipmakers can challenge Nvidia’s dominance.

“China doesn’t want Nvidia to sell GPUs to Chinese companies,” Luckey said. “There are Chinese companies that want to buy Nvidia GPUs… China will not give them an import permit because they want to build an internal domestic processor industry… not build one that is dependent on the United States.”.

Nvidia has said as much itself — the U.S. government granted the manufacturer license to ship some of its powerful H200 chips to certain Chinese customers, but those sales were restricted by the Chinese government. Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress said during the company’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that it will no longer sell H200 chips in China at all.

Luckey is far from alone among industry peers in his defense of Huang.

More than 200,000 people — including Elon Musk and the CEOs of Y Combinator, Databricks, Epic Games, Shopify, and Replit — have signed a petition calling for Nvidia to reinstate its founder. But Nvidia executives remarked during the firm’s earnings call on Tuesday that the company does not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.

XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail.
  • According to recent reports, A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem: a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y.
  • Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench, a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026.

According to recent reports, A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem: a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed.

Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal. Drawing on 8,115 real-world questions spanning programming and everyday activities such as cooking and home repair, we introduce a benchmark that measures whether models identify these misconceptions and are able to prioritize effective solutions in their responses.

The models we evaluated on XYBench – Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro – often suggested a solution to the user’s problem but kept their answers focused on the original, mistaken approach. Unlike human reference answers, all five models were less likely to steer owners away from that approach and toward a solution suited to their goal.

People use AI systems with different levels of knowledge and may not always know how best to approach a problem. We hope XYBench helps researchers measure whether model improvements make assistants better at recognizing mistaken assumptions, explaining why a proposed approach might not work, and suggesting more effective alternatives—even when users don't know the right questions to ask.

We built XYBench from four sources: 1,557 questions from Stack Overflow, 184 from Stack Exchange, 102 manually curated examples, and 6,272 questions generated from WikiHow guides. For each question, we identified the stated request (Y), what the person explicitly asks for, and the intended request (X)—the underlying goal that can be inferred from context.

Sources indicate that for the public forum questions, we used the three highest-scored human answers and the accepted answer, where available, to establish the intended request and possible solutions. We filtered out cases where answering the stated request was judged sufficient. For WikiHow, we used Sonnet 4.5 to generate questions around plausible misconceptions in procedural guides, then refined them to include enough context for an expert to infer the underlying goal without stating it outright. We removed examples where answering the literal request would largely resolve the problem.

A model might spend several paragraphs recommending a more powerful vacuum cleaner, then briefly suggest checking for a clogged hose. If a clog is causing the weak suction, clearing it could solve the problem.

Industry observers note that A more helpful answer would recognize that the user wants to restore suction and focus on diagnosing the cause. This draws on pragmatics, the branch of linguistics concerned with how context and communicative intent shape meaning. To test whether models use this understanding in their answers, XYBench measures three aspects of each response:.

In XYBench, Claude Sonnet 4.5 serves as the automated judge. It classifies individual suggestions within each model’s response and assesses the answer’s pragmatic emphasis.

It has been revealed that to validate Sonnet 4.5’s judgments, two human reviewers independently assessed 500 model responses to XYBench questions. Agreement with the judge, averaged across the reviewers, ranged from 97.5–100% on whether a solution appeared, 84.6–93.3% on misconception identification, and 74.2–79.8% on pragmatic emphasis.

It has been revealed that we evaluated Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro on XYBench in a single-turn setting, with one response per question. We evaluated human reference answers separately using the same metrics.

Across all four sources, every model was more likely to include a solution to the stated request (Y) than to the underlying goal (X). On Stack Overflow, stated-request solutions appeared in 75–86% of responses, compared with 59–71% for underlying-goal solutions.

A passing mention of a solution does not make it the focus of an answer. In the vacuum example, a model could briefly suggest unclogging the hose but focus most of its response on buying a more powerful vacuum. We would count that response as containing a solution to the underlying goal, even though the model emphasized the stated request. We measured overall emphasis separately: on Stack Overflow, models focused primarily on the underlying goal in only 35–41% of their responses, and on the stated request in 47–57%. In the remaining responses, models gave similar emphasis to the stated request and the underlying goal.

We also tested whether making the user’s goal explicit would help. In an oracle experiment, we supplied both the stated request (Y) and the intended request (X) alongside each question. On Stack Overflow, Sonnet 4.6’s rate of including a solution to the underlying goal rose from 59% to 67%, but its misconception-identification rate fell from 47% to 34%. Across the sources with human reference answers, every model in this experiment still trailed humans on misconception identification. Supplying intent helped, but did not consistently close the gap with human responses. This suggests that detecting intent is only part of the challenge: models also need to act on it when it diverges from the stated request.

A separate experiment tested whether models could identify useful advice when judging responses instead of writing them. We gave the same five models, plus GPT-4.1, each question with two possible answers: one focused on the literal request and one explaining the misconception and addressing the underlying goal. On Stack Overflow, all six chose the goal-focused answer in 71–84% of cases. By comparison, only 35–41% of the answers written by the five models in our main evaluation primarily focused on the underlying goal. The results expose a gap between recognizing useful advice and producing it, which a multiple-choice test alone would miss.

Sources indicate that researchers can use XYBench to test whether changes to prompting or training help models identify misconceptions, offer solutions to users’ underlying problems, and make those solutions the focus of their answers. Measuring each behavior individually lets researchers see whether progress in one also improves the others.

It has been revealed that future work could test which training methods help models act on inferred intent—AKA what owners need and not just what they literally asked for. The XYBench currently covers English-language queries and mainly procedural problems; extending it to other languages, cultures, and conversational settings remains an open direction.

We hope XYBench enables researchers to build models that offer useful advice even when a user’s first question rests on a mistaken assumption.

#59438. Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
